# Housekeeping: wasm-gates

## Authorized scope and smallest closable slice

Review the complete `tools/wasm-gates` Cargo package and its tests. Deliver practical, behavior-preserving cleanup in this package, or an evidenced no-change verdict when existing choices earn their cost. Cover all five user requests: repeated code/LoC; load-bearing test purposes; avoidable copies; applicable micro SIMD; and data structures that cap efficiency. The user requests two GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh agents concurrently; this overrides the default Terra implementation model for this workflow. Root Sol owns briefing, adversarial review, exact-path checkpoints, integration and remote synchronization.

## Frozen boundaries

Existing public APIs, feature behavior, canonical/wire identities, arithmetic order and per-lane rendered bits, latency/tail, link modes, smoothing and NaN/denormal rules remain contractual. Zero render allocations/frees, locks, I/O or syscalls; no runtime native ISA dispatch. Retain scalar tails, 4-lane Wasm/NEON and x86 AVX2/FMA. Preserve all feature and target configurations. Do not expand another open issue or change DSP algorithms. Read current related issue bodies before touching their subject; discoveries that require architecture or product decisions become bounded follow-ups and final owner questions.

## Implementation and test-value decisions

Prefer deleting or consolidating repetition to adding abstractions that increase total complexity. Assess every existing test or a clearly named homogeneous family by its plausible unique defect; remove trivial, redundant or obsolete cases only after identifying the surviving behavioral gate. Keep independent numeric/oracle, fault, allocation, queue, boundary and target tests. Add/rewrite tests only for a concrete uncovered defect, and state which plausible defect no existing test catches. No prose/source-grep tests, new bit-digest pins or exact resource-byte pins. Copies needed for ownership, snapshots or atomic admission stay unless the same semantics are proved with less work. Data structure changes must preserve deterministic order and bounded realtime work. Inspect applicable hot loops and generated code before claiming additional SIMD; recursive/stateful dependencies alone do not justify changing arithmetic.

## Objective gates and evidence

- Read all production and test files in this package; record concise findings for each of the five requests, concrete changed/deferred locations, and load-bearing test families with retained coverage for deletions.
- Run focused locked package tests and affected feature configurations; use existing downstream/RT/differential gates proportional to the changed contract. Check formatting and package clippy with warnings denied. Relevant Wasm and AArch64 compile checks are required for changed product code; record limitations candidly.
- Changes to DSP arithmetic or hot state need existing independent numeric and scalar/SIMD gates plus one-time base/head evidence when needed; no permanent comparison against the old implementation. Existing research remains the algorithm authority; no new algorithm or listening claim is authorized.
- Benchmarks are optional and descriptive. Any timed measurement freezes its workload/validator, passes zero-workload preflight, and runs exactly one invocation with one warmup/two measured rounds. No timing optimization loop, performance percentage or unsupported sound-quality claim.
- Root conducts one adversarial verdict per coherent attempt, at most five total attempts. Every new/rewritten test gets its unique-defect sentence in that verdict. No-change audits require the same five-axis review, not manufactured edits.
- Stop after a coherent compiling, focused-green tranche; root commits exact owned paths before further edits. Keep edits within `tools/wasm-gates` and this numbered spec. Independent crates use separate worktrees. Root pushes promptly and updates this GitHub issue with evidence; close only after PASS and evidence upstream, verifying remote state. Merge through the required qualification check and remove clean completed worktrees.

### Complete test purposes and independent ownership

| Existing function | Plausible defect / actual scope |
| --- | --- |
| `g5_native_digests_match_pins` | Any native case/width digest drift or nonzero minmax/f64/meter differential fails. This is the sole native replay owner of the delegated cross-target pins; actual native run covers 142 cases / 358 comparisons. |
| `g5_lane_corpus_is_finite` | Local lane-value extraction of wrong length or nonfinite kernel/elementwise/meter-peak output fails at its frame/width. It deliberately uses `has_lane_values`; delegated result-word corpora retain their own numerical laws. |
| `g5_case_digests_are_distinct` | Accidentally duplicated pinned computations fail with both names; only the documented idle-SVF equivalence is exempt. |
| `g5_idle_ramped_svf_equals_the_plain_svf` | An idle-ramp pin differing from its plain low-pass counterpart fails even if both independently match their own pins. Combined with native replay, this holds the current law at every available width. Same signals/search/order remain after raw comparison. |
| `g5_fma_case_is_unfused_and_the_case_is_not_vacuous` | A corpus that stops matching explicit multiply/add, or operands that cease separating the fused reference, fails. Both conditions and all widths/operands remain; native replay alone cannot prove operand nonvacuity. |
| `g5_delegated_cases_use_the_owning_crates_pins` | A copied/drifting owner pin, omitted family, changed width/name delegation, or inserted/reordered appended builtin indices fails. Existing owning-crate digest tables remain authoritative. |
| `g5_no_case_is_vacuously_zero` | Local lane-value cases that accidentally render only positive zero fail, while the one explicit subnormal one-pole flush case must stay positive zero. Distinctness alone could admit a newly zero case when no other case shared its digest. |
| `g6_full_wasm_gate_corpus_is_canonical_under_caller_ftz` | A wrong canonical FP guard fails full-corpus pins under caller FTZ/DAZ; the unguarded hostile arm must diverge in at least 16 rows, and the saved caller word must be restored. Canonical f64/meter counts are separately held to zero. |
| `g6_the_guard_is_an_identity_for_a_caller_who_never_set_ftz` | Guarded versus unguarded clear-word execution must retain every case/width digest and exact caller word. It independently checks transition identity over the full corpus. |
| Alternative `g6_full_wasm_gate_corpus_portable_smoke` | Existing cfg fallback checks nonempty corpus only, with no FP-control claim. It has no execution cost on the accepted x86/AArch64 branches and is retained under the frozen G6/target boundary; it was not built/run here. |

The nine active functions retain all original matrices and generators. The two edited assertion functions keep their distinct current-law/nonvacuity claims rather than comparing an old production body. G6 invokes the canonical guard around the corpus explicitly; it is not a new test of every production render entry or every possible caller rounding mode.

## Root adversarial verdict: REQUEST CHANGES — attempt 1

Root reviewed the complete four-path diff, actual native/guest/CLI/lint/release evidence and all test purposes. Reporter consolidation preserves fixed leg labels, field/literal/hex spelling and stdout/stderr order; direct array comparisons preserve idle law and FMA nonvacuity. The successful saved guest result is genuinely reused on the modified host, with no claim of a new failure-guest experiment. One bounded test-value correction remains. The alternative portable nonempty smoke has no cost on accepted x86/AArch64 host targets, but its useful coverage check is absent from the active clear-word identity gate: render_corpus returning an empty or incomplete vector in both arms would pass that gate.

Attempt 2 is authorized only in tests/g6_full_corpus_ftz.rs and concise evidence: remove the weak fallback function and add an independently derived full comparison count to the existing identity gate. The frozen corpus has scalar-only math and delay families; all remaining families run at every native width, so expected rows are `(CASE_COUNT - MATH_CASE_COUNT - DELAY_CASE_COUNT) * WIDTHS + MATH_CASE_COUNT + DELAY_CASE_COUNT`. Do not call native_report or render another corpus just to count rows. Keep the existing two-arm length/order/digest/FP-word checks, all inputs/guards and both active native functions unchanged otherwise.

Rewritten test value: omitting any replay rows, especially an empty helper result in both arms, must turn the active full-corpus identity owner red; comparing the two lengths alone cannot catch it. No new test function, fixture, numerical expression, target configuration, public API or corpus change. Focused native G6 debug/release tests, strict package lint and fmt/diff suffice for this test-only revision; reuse the complete attempt-1 product/guest/CLI/policy evidence candidly. Pause the exact G6 path at focused-green for root checkpoint before final evidence. This is one additional coherent revision and verdict, not a reopened matrix.
